doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Back on the road and the 881 Club in Los Angeles
summary: First jobs in Canada, Detroit and Minneapolis, then California and the 881 Club on La Cienega attracting stars.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: We were up in Hull, Canada, I remember that was one of the first jobs.

And after that we just — everywhere, Detroit, and up to St. Paul, Minneapolis, out to California, we were there for a long time. And out in California we were doing once again just piano and the two voices. And we were working in a place called John Walsh’s 88 Club?

881 Club. On LaCienega Blvd. And word got around and all of a sudden Mitzi Gaynor’s coming in, Cary Grant is coming in, Ray Milland is coming in, and everybody is coming in and we’re doing great business and it was wonderful.
And Bobby Troup. You know a lot of people who liked music started coming in there.
And that was good for a while. And pretty soon we started getting different bookings, and we’d get ourselves a group, a rhythm section, and yeah, we’re on the road.
